screening_population: clinically healthy newborns rooming-in with mother

study_target_definition_raw: screening for congenital heart disease broadly; no important cyanotic CHD found

screening_population: apparently healthy newborns at maternity ward
screening_timing_raw: median 2.5 h; range 0.5-7.5 h; repeats 0.5-1 h later
screening_algorithm_raw: pre/postductal POS; non-approved test triggered paediatric assessment
study_target_definition_raw: authors report one CCHD due pulmonary stenosis
diagnosis_categories_raw: pulmonary stenosis; TTN; infection/other treatment-requiring conditions; short NICU observation; assessment-only false positives
diagnosis_counts_raw: 1 pulmonary stenosis; 14 transitory tachypnoea; 10 other conditions requiring treatment; 18 NICU observation without treatment; 16 remained with mother after assessment
individual_diagnoses: one pulmonary stenosis; 14 TTN; 10 other treatment-requiring conditions; 18 observation only; 16 no further treatment
lesion_mapping_status: pulmonary valve stenosis is conditional harmonized CCHD and source does not report death or surgery/catheterization <=28 d
management_actionability_evidence: 18 infants were admitted to NICU for observation until saturation normalized; 25 infants required treatment, including the pulmonary-stenosis case. Thus CAN-A=42 if PS is harmonized CCHD and excluded, or 43 if it remains harmonized-negative. Sixteen had no further treatment after paediatric assessment and are aggregate NON_CAN.
entry_hold_reason: pulmonary-stenosis target mapping requires unavailable <=28-day timing
poolability_reason: bounded denominator and numerator are fully classified but no single primary-analysis weight can be assigned; additionally very-early screening is a major heterogeneity flag
source_full_text_provenance: Havelund KW et al. Dan Med J. 2019;66(11):A5576. PMID 31686645.
extraction_notes: Harmonized denominator 58-59; Strict=Expanded 42-43. Corresponding proportion is 72.4%-72.9%. Do not force pulmonary stenosis into or out of target without <=28-day evidence.

screening_timing_raw: SpO2 at 15 min and 6 h; only persistent abnormality at 6 h proceeded to echo
screening_algorithm_raw: SpO2 <95% at 15 min; reassessment at 6 h; persistent abnormality or >=3% limb difference -> echocardiography
study_target_definition_raw: authors classify TGA and tricuspid atresia as CCHD; four additional early PDA findings
diagnosis_categories_raw: TGA with severe PAH; tricuspid atresia with moderate PAH; early PDA/PFO findings
diagnosis_counts_raw: TGA1; tricuspid atresia1; PDA/PFO transitional findings4
individual_diagnoses: TGA+severe PAH; tricuspid atresia+moderate PAH; PFO+small closing PDA; moderate-large PDA+PFO; mild-moderate PDA; large PDA+severe PAH
lesion_mapping_status: TGA without reported structural complexity is mapped as simple TGA and therefore unconditional harmonized CCHD. Tricuspid atresia is not an automatic locked-target lesion and no early intervention/death equivalence is reported.
management_actionability_evidence: No treatment, escalation, altered disposition or required follow-up is documented for the tricuspid-atresia infant; diagnosis therefore CAN-U. Authors explicitly caution that the four PDA findings may be physiological transitional findings and no follow-up echo was performed; these are NON_CAN.
entry_hold_reason: inherited early/transitional lesion-mapping flag resolved in extraction
poolability_reason: complete participant-level terminal classification; retain very-early 6-hour screening as mandatory timing heterogeneity/sensitivity flag
source_full_text_provenance: Shah H et al. Cureus. 2026;18(5):e108873. PMID 42299162; PMCID PMC13264696; DOI 10.7759/cureus.108873.
extraction_notes: Strict 0/5; Expanded 1/5; NON_CAN transitional PDA/PFO 4/5. Seventy-five of 81 low saturations at 15 min normalized by 6 h and are PASS, not denominator.
